purpose: Factor-level RankIC stability diagnostics for training and validation. This analysis does not read test or final OOS data.

method.rank_ic: Daily cross-sectional Spearman correlation between each raw factor and its same-horizon forward total-return label.
method.aggregation: Simple time-series mean across daily RankIC observations; factor signs are not flipped or selected using validation.
method.annualized_ic_ir: ic_ir * sqrt(annualization_days), with 252 days by default. Overlapping labels mean this is a diagnostic, not an independent-observation annualization.
method.newey_west: Bartlett-kernel HAC t-statistic for the mean daily RankIC. The default lag is horizon - 1 trading days to account for overlapping forward labels. P-values use a two-sided normal approximation.
method.yearly_stability: The same daily RankIC metrics computed within each calendar year. Partial first and last years are labeled by their actual date range.
method.factor_correlation: Mean daily cross-sectional Spearman correlation for each factor pair. It measures redundancy, not predictive value.

limitations: Validation contains one narrow industry universe and a short market regime; train-to-validation sign changes are not sufficient for causal claims.
Overlapping 5/20-session labels induce serial dependence. Newey-West lags mitigate but do not eliminate this issue.
RankIC measures cross-sectional ordering, not executable returns after costs, capacity, or A-share trading constraints.
